"ROLE
You are a senior full-stack + ML engineer. Build a complete, working, 100% free AI Video @COMMENT_BODY@ Voice Dubbing web app, modeled on Sarvam Indus Creator Studio's \"Dubbing\" feature. No paid APIs, no API keys, no credit card. Everything must run on free/open-source tools.

GOAL
User uploads a video/audio file, picks source language and one or more target languages, and gets back a dubbed video (MP4), dubbed audio (MP3), and subtitles (SRT), with the original background music preserved and timing matched.

TECH STACK (free only)
- Frontend: Next.js + Tailwind, mobile-first, clean white UI, collapsible sidebar
- Backend: Python FastAPI, background worker (Celery + Redis, or simple threaded queue), SQLite
- Audio extraction and merge: FFmpeg
- Vocal/background split: Demucs
- Speech-to-text: faster-whisper (word timestamps, language auto-detect)
- Speaker detection: pyannote.audio (fallback: user-selected 1-5 speakers)
- Translation: IndicTrans2 for Indian languages, NLLB-200 as fallback
- Text-to-speech: edge-tts (primary, free), AI4Bharat Indic-Parler-TTS (offline option)
- Voice cloning (optional toggle): OpenVoice or XTTS-v2
- Time fitting: FFmpeg atempo / pyrubberband
- Hosting: Hugging Face Spaces / Render free tier; GPU work on Google Colab + ngrok

LANGUAGES
Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Urdu, English (source auto-detect + multi-select targets).

PAGES
1. Dubbing dashboard
   - Sidebar: Home, Text to Speech, Dubbing, Voice Library, Voice Cloning, Speech to Text, Usage, Docs
   - Top bar: free minutes left, feedback button, \"+\" new dub button
   - Table: thumbnail, name, source language, target language chip, created date, status badge (Queued / Processing / Completed / Failed), download menu
   - Search box, status filter, pagination (\"1-7 of N\")
2. \"Create a dub\" modal
   - Upload / Record tabs (drag-and-drop; max 2GB or 1 hour)
   - Source language (with Auto-detect), number of speakers (1-5), multi-select target languages
   - Advanced options: keep background music, voice cloning on/off, voice gender, speech speed, burn-in subtitles, glossary of words to keep untranslated
   - Cancel and Create dub buttons
3. Progress screen: live steps (Extract audio, Separate vocals, Transcribe, Translate, Generate voice, Sync, Merge) with percentage and ETA
4. Result page: player with Original / Dubbed toggle, side-by-side editable transcript and translation, per-segment \"Regenerate voice\", downloads (MP4, MP3, SRT, VTT)
5. Usage page: free minutes used/left (30 min/day, resets daily)

PIPELINE
upload, then FFmpeg extract audio, then Demucs split (vocals/background), then faster-whisper transcript with timestamps, then merge into sentence segments, then translate each segment with context, then TTS per segment, then time-stretch each clip to fit its original slot (max 1.25x, else shorten the translation), then mix with background at the original loudness, then mux into the video, then save and notify.

QUALITY RULES
- Keep names, brands, and numbers correct; support a do-not-translate glossary
- No clipping or overlapping speech; normalize loudness (-16 LUFS)
- Keep lip/pause timing natural; preserve silence gaps
- Process long files in chunks so the free tier does not time out
- Clear error messages and retry on failure; delete temp files after processing

NON-FUNCTIONAL
- Fully responsive for phone screens (touch-friendly, large buttons)
- Dark/light toggle
- Rate limit: 30 free minutes/day per user (cookie or simple login)
- Add a consent checkbox for voice cloning (\"I have the rights to this voice\")

DELIVERABLES
1. Folder structure
2. Complete backend and frontend code (no placeholders, no \"TODO\")
3. requirements.txt, package.json, Dockerfile, .env.example
4. Step-by-step local setup + free deployment guide (Hugging Face Spaces / Render / Colab)
5. A Gradio single-file MVP first, so I can test the pipeline immediately, then the full UI

BUILD ORDER
Step 1: working Gradio MVP of the pipeline. Step 2: FastAPI backend. Step 3: dashboard, modal, progress, result pages. Step 4: usage limits and polish. After each step, tell me how to run and test it.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

# Skill: OpenCode

# OpenCode

Use this guide as the starting point for work involving OpenCode itself. It
covers the core concepts needed to configure and customize OpenCode, extend it
with plugins, and build integrations with the OpenCode SDK, clients, and API.

Full documentation is available at <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/>. This overview is
only an index of core concepts. Before answering a question about a topic below,
fetch the URL named in that section and use the full page as the source of
truth. Follow links from that page when the question needs more detail. Fetch
<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> first when you need to discover the relevant
documentation page.

A machine-readable documentation index is available at
<https://opencode.ai/v2/llms.txt>.

## Version policy

Always answer for OpenCode V2 unless the user explicitly asks about V1,
legacy OpenCode, or migrating from V1.

Use only <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> documentation as the source of truth for V2.
Do not use <https://opencode.ai/docs/>, which documents V1, and do not use
general web search to resolve a V2 documentation question when the V2 docs or
linked pages cover it. The schema served from
<https://opencode.ai/config.json> accepts both V2 fields and deprecated V1
fields. Never recommend a field it marks deprecated. If V2 documentation is
missing or contradictory, state the uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of falling back to V1.

V1 documentation and syntax may be consulted only when the user explicitly
asks about V1 or when needed as migration input. Outputs and recommendations
must still use V2 unless the user specifically requests a V1 result.

## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Config changes apply without a restart. OpenCode watches config files and
reloads agents, commands, skills, MCP servers, and plugins after a save. The TUI
does the same for `cli.json`. To force a full reload, use `/reload`. Don't tell
the user to restart OpenCode after editing config.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/www/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. Restart it only if it is stuck or unhealthy, not to apply
configuration changes:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

Use OpenCode's built-in `api` command for local requests. It uses the same
discovery and authentication flow as the TUI and may start the background
service when no compatible healthy service is available. It accepts either an
HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:

```sh
opencode api post /api/example --data '{"key":"value"}'
opencode api get /api/example --header 'X-Example:value'
```

Request bodies default to `Content-Type: application/json`. When OpenCode is
connected to an explicit server instead of its managed background service, use
the same configured server and authentication context rather than constructing
an unauthenticated request separately.

See the [full API reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api) for available
endpoints, parameters, request bodies, and response schemas. The
raw [OpenAPI specification](https://opencode.ai/v2/openapi.json) is also
available for code generation and other tooling.

## [Client](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client)

For questions about connecting an application to OpenCode over the network,
fetch the full [client guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client) before
answering.

`@opencode/client` is the generated TypeScript client for the OpenCode HTTP
API. Its methods and types come from the same contract as the API reference.
The default entrypoint exposes Promise-based resource clients and async
iterables for streaming endpoints. The `@opencode/client/effect` entrypoint
exposes typed Effects, Streams, and decoded OpenCode schema values. Its
`Service` API can discover, start, stop, and authenticate with the local
background service from a Node application.

## [SDK](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk)

For questions about embedding OpenCode directly in an application, fetch the
full [SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk) before answering. The SDK
hosts OpenCode in the application without opening an HTTP listener.

Use the [Effect SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/effect) for
Effect applications. For Cloudflare Durable Objects, use the
[Cloudflare SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/cloudflare).

## [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)

OpenCode runs a client and a background server. Start by determining whether a
problem belongs to the client, the shared server, or one project.

- Check the service with `opencode service status` and verify the API with
  `opencode api get /api/info`.
- Compare with `opencode --standalone`, which runs the TUI with a private
  server, to isolate shared-service issues.
- Inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. Filter `role=cli` for
  client startup and `role=server` for sessions, providers, plugins,
  permissions, and tools.
- Run one reproduction with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` when normal logs are not
  sufficient.
- Do not delete or edit the database, service registration, or service config
  while diagnosing a problem. Back up persistent data before inspecting it
  with external tools.
- Redact API keys, authorization headers, prompts, file contents, and other
  sensitive data before sharing diagnostics.

See the [full troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)
for service lifecycle commands, API inspection, log locations, explicit server
connections, issue-reporting details, and local development paths.

Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
STORAGE = Path(os.getenv("DUB_STORAGE", ROOT / "storage")).resolve()
STORAGE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

LANGUAGES = {
    "Hindi": ("hi", "hin_Deva", "hi-IN-SwaraNeural", "hi-IN-MadhurNeural"),
    "Kannada": ("kn", "kan_Knda", "kn-IN-SapnaNeural", "kn-IN-GaganNeural"),
    "Tamil": ("ta", "tam_Taml", "ta-IN-PallaviNeural", "ta-IN-ValluvarNeural"),
    "Telugu": ("te", "tel_Telu", "te-IN-ShrutiNeural", "te-IN-MohanNeural"),
    "Malayalam": ("ml", "mal_Mlym", "ml-IN-SobhanaNeural", "ml-IN-MidhunNeural"),
    "Marathi": ("mr", "mar_Deva", "mr-IN-AarohiNeural", "mr-IN-ManoharNeural"),
    "Bengali": ("bn", "ben_Beng", "bn-IN-TanishaaNeural", "bn-IN-BashkarNeural"),
    "Gujarati": ("gu", "gujr_Gujr", "gu-IN-DhwaniNeural", "gu-IN-NiranjanNeural"),
    "Punjabi": ("pa", "pan_Guru", "pa-IN-VaaniNeural", "pa-IN-OjasNeural"),
    "Odia": ("or", "ory_Orya", "or-IN-SubhasiniNeural", "or-IN-SukantNeural"),
    "Urdu": ("ur", "urd_Arab", "ur-PK-UzmaNeural", "ur-PK-AsadNeural"),
    "English": ("en", "eng_Latn", "en-US-AvaNeural", "en-US-AndrewNeural"),
}

class PipelineError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def run(command: list[str], *, timeout: int = 3600) -> str:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise PipelineError(f"Required program is missing: {command[0]}. Install FFmpeg and ensure it is on PATH.") from exc
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        raise PipelineError(f"Processing timed out while running {Path(command[0]).name}.") from exc
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        detail = (exc.stderr or exc.stdout or str(exc)).strip().splitlines()[-8:]
        raise PipelineError("Processing command failed: " + "\n".join(detail)) from exc
    return result.stdout.strip()


def probe_duration(path: Path) -> float:
    raw = run(["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries", "format=duration", "-of", "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", str(path)])
    try:
        return float(raw)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise PipelineError("Could not read the media duration. Please upload a valid audio or video file.") from exc


def segments_from_words(words: list[Any], transcript: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    segments: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    chunk: list[Any] = []
    for word in words:
        chunk.append(word)
        text = str(getattr(word, "word", "")).strip()
        gap = getattr(word, "start", 0) - getattr(chunk[-2], "end", 0) if len(chunk) > 1 else 0
        if (re.search(r"[.!?。؟।]$", text) and len(chunk) >= 3) or gap > 0.9 or len(chunk) >= 22:
            segments.append(_word_segment(chunk))
            chunk = []
    if chunk:
        segments.append(_word_segment(chunk))
    if not segments and transcript.strip():
        segments = [{"start": 0.0, "end": 0.0, "text": transcript.strip()}]
    return segments


def _word_segment(words: list[Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "start": max(0.0, float(getattr(words[0], "start", 0))),
        "end": max(float(getattr(words[0], "start", 0)) + 0.1, float(getattr(words[-1], "end", 0))),
        "text": " ".join(str(getattr(word, "word", "")).strip() for word in words).strip(),
    }


class Translator:
    _lock = threading.Lock()
    _instance: "Translator | None" = None

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        try:
            from transformers import AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM, AutoTokenizer
            import torch
        except ImportError as exc:
            raise PipelineError("Translation needs the optional AI packages. Install them with: pip install -r requirements-ai.txt") from exc
        model_name = os.getenv("NLLB_MODEL", "facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M")
        try:
            self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
            self.model = AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained(model_name)
            self.torch = torch
        except Exception as exc:
            raise PipelineError(f"Could not load the free NLLB translation model ({model_name}): {exc}") from exc

    @classmethod
    def get(cls) -> "Translator":
        with cls._lock:
            if cls._instance is None:
                cls._instance = cls()
            return cls._instance

    def translate(self, text: str, source: str, target: str, glossary: list[str]) -> str:
        if source not in LANGUAGES or target not in LANGUAGES:
            raise PipelineError("Choose a supported source and target language.")
        source_code, target_code = LANGUAGES[source][1], LANGUAGES[target][1]
        protected: dict[str, str] = {}
        working = text
        for index, term in enumerate(sorted(set(glossary), key=len, reverse=True)):
            term = term.strip()
            if term:
                marker = f"ZZZKEEP{index}TOKENZZZ"
                working = re.sub(re.escape(term), marker, working, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
                protected[marker] = term
        try:
            self.tokenizer.src_lang = source_code
            inputs = self.tokenizer(working, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512)
            generated = self.model.generate(**inputs, forced_bos_token_id=self.tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(target_code), max_new_tokens=512)
            result = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(generated, skip_special_tokens=True)[0]
        except Exception as exc:
            raise PipelineError(f"Translation failed for {target}: {exc}") from exc
        for marker, term in protected.items():
            result = result.replace(marker, term).replace(marker.lower(), term)
        return result.strip()


def transcribe(audio_path: Path, source_language: str) -> tuple[str, str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    try:
        from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise PipelineError("Speech recognition needs faster-whisper. Install it with: pip install -r requirements-ai.txt") from exc
    model_name = os.getenv("WHISPER_MODEL", "small")
    device = os.getenv("WHISPER_DEVICE", "cpu")
    compute = os.getenv("WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE", "int8" if device == "cpu" else "float16")
    try:
        model = WhisperModel(model_name, device=device, compute_type=compute)
        language = None if source_language == "Auto-detect" else LANGUAGES[source_language][0]
        pieces, info = model.transcribe(str(audio_path), language=language, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True, beam_size=5)
        words = []
        texts = []
        for piece in pieces:
            texts.append(piece.text.strip())
            words.extend(piece.words or [])
        text = " ".join(part for part in texts if part).strip()
        found_language = next((name for name, row in LANGUAGES.items() if row[0] == info.language), info.language)
        return text, found_language, segments_from_words(words, text)
    except PipelineError:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        raise PipelineError(f"Speech recognition failed: {exc}") from exc


async def synthesize(text: str, voice: str, path: Path, rate: int = 0) -> None:
    try:
        import edge_tts
        communicate = edge_tts.Communicate(text, voice, rate=f"{rate:+d}%")
        await communicate.save(str(path))
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise PipelineError("Text-to-speech needs edge-tts. Install it with: pip install -r requirements-ai.txt") from exc
    except Exception as exc:
        raise PipelineError(f"Voice generation failed. Check your internet connection and try again: {exc}") from exc


def write_subtitles(segments: list[dict[str, Any]], path: Path, vtt: bool = False) -> None:
    def stamp(seconds: float, comma: bool) -> str:
        ms = max(0, round(seconds * 1000))
        h, ms = divmod(ms, 3_600_000)
        m, ms = divmod(ms, 60_000)
        s, ms = divmod(ms, 1000)
        return f"{h:02}:{m:02}:{s:02}{',' if comma else '.'}{ms:03}"
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
        if vtt:
            file.write("WEBVTT\n\n")
        for i, segment in enumerate(segments, 1):
            file.write(f"{i}\n" if not vtt else "")
            file.write(f"{stamp(segment['start'], not vtt)} --> {stamp(segment['end'], not vtt)}\n{segment['translation']}\n\n")


def _split_vocals(audio: Path, temp: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path | None]:
    try:
        import demucs  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:
        return audio, None
    run([os.getenv("PYTHON", "python"), "-m", "demucs", "--two-stems=vocals", "-n", os.getenv("DEMUCS_MODEL", "htdemucs"), "-o", str(temp / "stems"), str(audio)], timeout=7200)
    output = temp / "stems" / os.getenv("DEMUCS_MODEL", "htdemucs") / audio.stem
    vocals, accompaniment = output / "vocals.wav", output / "no_vocals.wav"
    if not vocals.exists() or not accompaniment.exists():
        raise PipelineError("Demucs finished but its vocal/accompaniment stems were not found.")
    return vocals, accompaniment


def process_media(
    input_path: Path,
    output_dir: Path,
    source_language: str,
    targets: list[str],
    options: dict[str, Any],
    progress: Callable[[str, int, str], None] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    job_tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="dub-", dir=STORAGE))
    emit = progress or (lambda _step, _percent, _message: None)
    try:
        duration = probe_duration(input_path)
        if duration > 3600:
            raise PipelineError("Files must be one hour or shorter.")
        emit("Extract audio", 8, "Extracting a clean audio track with FFmpeg")
        source_wav = job_tmp / "source.wav"
        run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(input_path), "-vn", "-ac", "2", "-ar", "44100", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", str(source_wav)])
        emit("Separate vocals", 20, "Separating dialogue from background audio" if options.get("keep_music") else "Preparing dialogue track")
        vocals, background = _split_vocals(source_wav, job_tmp) if options.get("keep_music") else (source_wav, None)
        if options.get("keep_music") and background is None:
            raise PipelineError("Background music preservation requires Demucs. Install it with: pip install -r requirements-ai.txt")
        emit("Transcribe", 33, "Recognizing speech and word-level timing")
        transcript, detected_language, segments = transcribe(vocals, source_language)
        if not segments:
            raise PipelineError("No speech was detected. Try a clearer file or a different source language.")
        original_lang = detected_language if source_language == "Auto-detect" else source_language
        emit("Translate", 48, f"Translating {len(segments)} timed speech segments")
        translator = Translator.get()
        glossary = [part.strip() for part in str(options.get("glossary", "")).split(",") if part.strip()]
        for segment in segments:
            segment["translation"] = {}
            for target in targets:
                segment["translation"][target] = translator.translate(segment["text"], original_lang, target, glossary)
        result_files: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        for target_index, target in enumerate(targets):
            emit("Generate voice", 56 + int(22 * target_index / max(1, len(targets))), f"Generating {target} voice clips")
            target_dir = output_dir / target.lower()
            target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            _, _, female_voice, male_voice = LANGUAGES[target]
            voice = female_voice if options.get("voice_gender", "Female") == "Female" else male_voice
            clip_files: list[Path] = []
            slot_lengths: list[float] = []
            for index, segment in enumerate(segments):
                clip = job_tmp / f"{target_index}-{index}.mp3"
                slot = max(0.18, min(duration - segment["start"], segment["end"] - segment["start"] + 0.12))
                text = segment["translation"][target]
                awaitable = synthesize(text, voice, clip, int((float(options.get("speech_speed", 1)) - 1) * 100))
                asyncio.run(awaitable)
                clip_len = probe_duration(clip)
                if clip_len > slot * 1.25:
                    words = text.split()
                    while len(words) > 2 and clip_len > slot * 1.25:
                        words = words[:-1]
                        text = " ".join(words).rstrip(" ,;:") + "…"
                        asyncio.run(synthesize(text, voice, clip, int((float(options.get("speech_speed", 1)) - 1) * 100)))
                        clip_len = probe_duration(clip)
                    segment["translation"][target] = text
                fit_rate = min(1.25, max(1.0, clip_len / slot))
                normalized_clip = job_tmp / f"fit-{target_index}-{index}.wav"
                run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(clip), "-filter:a", f"atempo={fit_rate:.4f},apad,atrim=duration={slot:.3f}", "-ac", "2", "-ar", "44100", str(normalized_clip)])
                clip_files.append(normalized_clip)
                slot_lengths.append(slot)
            emit("Sync", 83 + int(7 * target_index / max(1, len(targets))), f"Fitting {target} speech to the original pauses")
            # Build the speech timeline with one delayed, padded input per segment. Each clip is
            # trimmed to its own slot, so adjacent words can never overlap.
            filter_parts = []
            inputs = []
            for i, (clip, segment, slot) in enumerate(zip(clip_files, segments, slot_lengths)):
                inputs += ["-i", str(clip)]
                delay = int(segment["start"] * 1000)
                filter_parts.append(f"[{i}:a]adelay={delay}|{delay},apad,atrim=duration={duration:.3f}[a{i}]")
            labels = "".join(f"[a{i}]" for i in range(len(clip_files)))
            filter_parts.append(f"{labels}amix=inputs={len(clip_files)}:duration=longest:normalize=0,alimiter=limit=0.95,dynaudnorm=f=150:g=7,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11[dub]")
            dub_audio = target_dir / f"dubbed-{target.lower()}.mp3"
            run(["ffmpeg", "-y", *inputs, "-filter_complex", ";".join(filter_parts), "-map", "[dub]", "-t", f"{duration:.3f}", "-codec:a", "libmp3lame", "-q:a", "2", str(dub_audio)])
            if background:
                mixed = target_dir / "mixed.wav"
                run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(dub_audio), "-i", str(background), "-filter_complex", "[1:a]volume=0.8[bg];[0:a][bg]amix=inputs=2:duration=longest:normalize=0,loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11[out]", "-map", "[out]", "-t", f"{duration:.3f}", str(mixed)])
                run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(mixed), "-codec:a", "libmp3lame", "-q:a", "2", str(dub_audio)])
            emit("Merge", 94, "Muxing dubbed audio and writing subtitle files")
            mp4 = target_dir / f"dubbed-{target.lower()}.mp4"
            run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", str(input_path), "-i", str(dub_audio), "-map", "0:v?", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-shortest", str(mp4)])
            srt, vtt = target_dir / f"subtitles-{target.lower()}.srt", target_dir / f"subtitles-{target.lower()}.vtt"
            write_subtitles([{**s, "translation": s["translation"][target]} for s in segments], srt)
            write_subtitles([{**s, "translation": s["translation"][target]} for s in segments], vtt, True)
            result_files[target] = {"mp4": str(mp4), "mp3": str(dub_audio), "srt": str(srt), "vtt": str(vtt)}
        emit("Completed", 100, "Your dubbed files are ready")
        return {"duration": duration, "detected_language": detected_language, "transcript": transcript, "segments": segments, "outputs": result_files}
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(job_tmp, ignore_errors=True)

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a free/open-source AI video and audio dubbing app modeled on Sarvam Indus Creator Studio, with a working Gradio MVP first and then a FastAPI backend and responsive Next.js UI.
- The user also asked to “Build a complete, playable game now”; this conflicts with the detailed dubbing-app requirements and has not been resolved.

## Requirements
- No paid APIs, API keys, or credit card; use open-source/free tools.
- Upload media, select source and multiple target languages, preserve background music, match speech timing, and provide dubbed MP4/MP3 plus SRT/VTT.
- Include a dashboard, create-dub modal, progress view, editable result/transcript UI, daily 30-minute quota, responsive layout, dark/light toggle, and voice-cloning rights consent.
- Deliver Gradio single-file MVP, full app code, `requirements.txt`, `package.json`, Dockerfile, `.env.example`, and local/free deployment instructions.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Prioritized the detailed dubbing-app scope; repository had no existing game implementation.
- Implemented FastAPI with a threaded job executor and SQLite, plus a Next.js frontend.
- AI dependencies are separated into `requirements-ai.txt` (not yet created); the core backend is designed to report helpful errors when optional AI packages are missing.
- Work is uncommitted.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the repository; it contained only starter scripts/docs, no app code.
- Created `backend/pipeline.py` with FFmpeg extraction/muxing, optional Demucs vocal separation, faster-whisper transcription, NLLB translation/glossary protection, edge-tts synthesis, time fitting, SRT/VTT generation, and per-target-language output generation.
- Created `backend/main.py` with FastAPI endpoints for health, languages, usage, job upload/status/results/downloads, editable segments, and job deletion; uses SQLite and a threaded executor.
- Created initial Next.js configuration, layout, global styling, API helpers, and sidebar components.

### Active
- Continue building frontend interactions: dashboard, upload/record modal, job polling/progress, result editing/playback/downloads, usage/docs pages, theme toggle.
- Fix and test backend/frontend integration; implement any incomplete behavior identified during review.
- Create Gradio MVP, requirements files, Dockerfile, `.env.example`, setup/deployment guide, and root folder structure documentation.

### Blocked
- No external blocker; remaining work is substantial.
- User’s final “playable game” line conflicts with the detailed dubbing-app request; assistant chose the dubbing app without clarification.

## Next Move
1. Continue with frontend components/page and complete the user-facing workflow.
2. Add the single-file Gradio MVP and packaging/deployment files.
3. Run Python syntax/import checks and frontend install/build; fix issues and report accurate run/test instructions.

## Relevant Files
- `backend/pipeline.py`: Core dubbing pipeline.
- `backend/main.py`: FastAPI API, SQLite job/usage handling, threaded worker.
- `frontend/app/globals.css`: Responsive styling and dark-mode styles.
- `frontend/app/layout.tsx`: Next.js root layout/metadata.
- `frontend/package.json`: Frontend dependencies and scripts.
- `frontend/lib/api.ts`: API types, language/step constants, fetch helpers.
- `frontend/components/Sidebar.tsx`: Sidebar navigation and quota display.
- `frontend/tsconfig.json`: TypeScript configuration.
- `frontend/next.config.mjs`: Next.js config.

134: def transcribe(audio_path: Path, source_language: str) -> tuple[str, str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
135:     try:
136:         from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
137:     except ImportError as exc:
138:         raise PipelineError("Speech recognition needs faster-whisper. Install it with: pip install -r requirements-ai.txt") from exc
139:     model_name = os.getenv("WHISPER_MODEL", "small")
140:     device = os.getenv("WHISPER_DEVICE", "cpu")
141:     compute = os.getenv("WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE", "int8" if device == "cpu" else "float16")
142:     try:
143:         model = WhisperModel(model_name, device=device, compute_type=compute)
144:         language = None if source_language == "Auto-detect" else LANGUAGES[source_language][0]
145:         pieces, info = model.transcribe(str(audio_path), language=language, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True, beam_size=5)
146:         words = []
147:         texts = []
148:         for piece in pieces:
149:             texts.append(piece.text.strip())
150:             words.extend(piece.words or [])
151:         text = " ".join(part for part in texts if part).strip()
152:         found_language = next((name for name, row in LANGUAGES.items() if row[0] == info.language), info.language)
153:         return text, found_language, segments_from_words(words, text)
154:     except PipelineError:
155:         raise
156:     except Exception as exc:

172:     def stamp(seconds: float, comma: bool) -> str:
173:         ms = max(0, round(seconds * 1000))
174:         h, ms = divmod(ms, 3_600_000)
175:         m, ms = divmod(ms, 60_000)
176:         s, ms = divmod(ms, 1000)
177:         return f"{h:02}:{m:02}:{s:02}{',' if comma else '.'}{ms:03}"
178:     with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
179:         if vtt:
180:             file.write("WEBVTT\n\n")
181:         for i, segment in enumerate(segments, 1):
182:             file.write(f"{i}\n" if not vtt else "")
183:             file.write(f"{stamp(segment['start'], not vtt)} --> {stamp(segment['end'], not vtt)}\n{segment['translation']}\n\n")

192:     output = temp / "stems" / os.getenv("DEMUCS_MODEL", "htdemucs") / audio.stem
193:     vocals, accompaniment = output / "vocals.wav", output / "no_vocals.wav"
194:     if not vocals.exists() or not accompaniment.exists():

218:         vocals, background = _split_vocals(source_wav, job_tmp) if options.get("keep_music") else (source_wav, None)
219:         if options.get("keep_music") and background is None:

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a free, open-source AI video/audio dubbing app, starting with a Gradio MVP and a FastAPI backend with a responsive Next.js UI.
- A separate request to “Build a complete, playable game now” conflicts with the detailed dubbing-app scope.

## Requirements
- No paid APIs, API keys, or credit card; use free/open-source tools.
- Support media upload, source and multiple target languages, background-music preservation, timed dubbing, MP4/MP3 and SRT/VTT downloads.
- Include dashboard, create-dub flow, progress, editable transcript/results, daily 30-minute quota, responsive layout, theme toggle, and voice-cloning rights consent.
- Deliver Gradio MVP, full app code, dependency manifests, Dockerfile, `.env.example`, and local/free deployment instructions.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Prioritized the dubbing app over the conflicting game request; the repository had no game implementation.
- Built a FastAPI backend with SQLite and threaded job execution, plus a Next.js frontend.
- Optional AI packages are intended to be separate from core backend dependencies.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented `backend/pipeline.py` for FFmpeg media processing, optional Demucs vocal separation, faster-whisper transcription, NLLB translation/glossary protection, edge-tts synthesis, timing, subtitles, and per-language output.
- Implemented `backend/main.py` endpoints for health, languages, usage/quota, jobs, upload, status/results/downloads, segment editing, and deletion.
- Added Next.js configuration, layout, API helpers, sidebar, dashboard and job-detail workflow, upload/record modal, progress view, transcript editing UI, downloads, informational pages, theme persistence, and supplemental styles.

### Active
- Complete Gradio MVP and packaging/deployment files: AI/core requirements, Dockerfile, `.env.example`, and setup documentation.
- Review/fix frontend and backend integration; run Python checks and frontend install/build.
- Verify and address functional gaps, including subtitle outputs after transcript edits and voice-cloning UI/backend behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add the single-file Gradio MVP and the missing dependencies, Dockerfile, `.env.example`, and deployment documentation.
2. Run Python syntax/import checks and frontend install/build; fix integration or type errors.
3. Review subtitle editing and voice cloning behavior, then document known limitations and accurate run instructions.

## Relevant Files
- `backend/pipeline.py`: Core media dubbing pipeline.
- `backend/main.py`: FastAPI API, SQLite jobs/quota, threaded worker.
- `frontend/app/page.tsx`: Dashboard, progress, results, transcript editor, and informational pages.
- `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`: Upload/record and dub configuration modal.
- `frontend/app/globals.css`: Existing styling and responsive/theme additions.
- `frontend/lib/api.ts`: API types and request helpers.
- `frontend/components/Sidebar.tsx`: Navigation and quota display.
- `frontend/package.json`: Frontend dependencies and scripts.
- `README.md`: Still contains generic starter content; replace with project setup/deployment guide.

## Important Context
- Backend defaults to port `8000`; frontend runs on port `3000` and defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
- AI model/package loading occurs at runtime; FFmpeg/ffprobe are required, and background-music preservation requires Demucs.
- Voice cloning is not implemented; the new modal explicitly indicates that enabling it still uses standard generated voices.
- Segment edits currently update stored job segments only; generated SRT/VTT files and audio are not regenerated by the save endpoint.

"""Single-file Gradio MVP for local audio/video dubbing."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import gradio as gr

from backend.pipeline import LANGUAGES, PipelineError, process_media


def dub_media(
    media: str | None,
    source_language: str,
    target_language: str,
    voice_gender: str,
    speech_speed: float,
    keep_music: bool,
    burn_subtitles: bool,
    glossary: str,
) -> tuple[str, str | None, str | None, str | None, str | None, str]:
    if not media:
        raise gr.Error("Upload an audio or video file first.")
    source = Path(media)
    job_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="voxora-gradio-"))
    input_path = job_dir / f"input{source.suffix.lower()}"
    shutil.copyfile(source, input_path)
    output_dir = job_dir / "outputs"
    try:
        result: dict[str, Any] = process_media(
            input_path,
            output_dir,
            source_language,
            [target_language],
            {
                "speakers": 1,
                "keep_music": keep_music,
                "voice_gender": voice_gender,
                "speech_speed": speech_speed,
                "burn_subtitles": burn_subtitles,
                "glossary": glossary,
            },
        )
        files = result["outputs"][target_language]
        # Return named files from a persistent directory; Gradio serves them for download.
        transcript = "\n".join(
            f"[{segment['start']:.2f}–{segment['end']:.2f}] {segment['text']}\n"
            f"→ {segment['translation'][target_language]}"
            for segment in result["segments"]
        )
        return (
            transcript,
            files.get("mp4"),
            files.get("mp3"),
            files.get("srt"),
            files.get("vtt"),
            f"Detected source language: {result['detected_language']}",
        )
    except PipelineError as exc:
        shutil.rmtree(job_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        raise gr.Error(str(exc)) from exc
    except Exception as exc:
        shutil.rmtree(job_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        raise gr.Error(f"Dubbing failed: {exc}") from exc


with gr.Blocks(title="Voxora — Open Dubbing Studio", theme=gr.themes.Soft()) as demo:
    gr.Markdown(
        "# Voxora Dubbing Studio\n"
        "Free, local-first audio and video dubbing. Models download on first use; "
        "Edge TTS needs an internet connection."
    )
    with gr.Row():
        with gr.Column(scale=1):
            media = gr.File(
                label="Audio or video file",
                file_count="single",
                type="filepath",
                file_types=[".mp4", ".mov", ".mkv", ".webm", ".avi", ".mp3", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".ogg", ".flac"],
            )
            source = gr.Dropdown(["Auto-detect", *LANGUAGES], value="Auto-detect", label="Source language")
            target = gr.Dropdown(list(LANGUAGES), value="Hindi", label="Dub into")
            gender = gr.Radio(["Female", "Male"], value="Female", label="Generated voice")
            speed = gr.Slider(0.75, 1.25, value=1, step=0.05, label="Speech speed")
            keep_music = gr.Checkbox(value=False, label="Preserve background music (requires Demucs)")
            burn = gr.Checkbox(value=False, label="Burn subtitles into video")
            glossary = gr.Textbox(label="Glossary (comma-separated, optional)")
            run_button = gr.Button("Create dub", variant="primary")
        with gr.Column(scale=2):
            status = gr.Markdown()
            transcript = gr.Textbox(label="Transcript and translation", lines=12, interactive=False)
            video = gr.Video(label="Dubbed video")
            audio = gr.Audio(label="Dubbed audio", type="filepath")
            with gr.Row():
                srt = gr.File(label="Download SRT")
                vtt = gr.File(label="Download VTT")
    run_button.click(
        dub_media,
        inputs=[media, source, target, gender, speed, keep_music, burn, glossary],
        outputs=[transcript, video, audio, srt, vtt, status],
    )
    gr.Markdown(
        "**Limits:** 2 GB / 60 minutes per file. Voice cloning is not included. "
        "Use only voices and media you have rights to use."
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo.queue().launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=7860)

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a free, open-source AI audio/video dubbing app with a Gradio MVP, FastAPI backend, and responsive Next.js UI.
- Complete packaging and deployment documentation, then verify the app and fix integration issues.

## Requirements
- Use free/open-source tools; no paid APIs, API keys, or credit card.
- Support media upload, multiple target languages, music preservation, timed dubbing, MP4/MP3 and SRT/VTT downloads, transcript editing, quota tracking, responsive UI, themes, and voice-rights consent.
- Deliver the Gradio MVP, full app code, dependency manifests, Docker setup, `.env.example`, and local/free deployment instructions.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Prioritize the dubbing app over the conflicting request to build a game; no game implementation was present.
- Use FastAPI with SQLite and threaded jobs, plus a Next.js frontend; keep AI packages separate from lightweight requirements.
- Voice cloning is not implemented; the UI discloses that standard generated voices are used.
- Transcript edits now regenerate downloadable SRT/VTT captions, but do not regenerate audio or subtitles already burned into video.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the dubbing pipeline and FastAPI API, including upload, jobs, quota, results, downloads, deletion, and segment editing.
- Added the Next.js dashboard, create-dub flow, progress/results views, transcript editor, theme toggle, and responsive styling.
- Added `gradio_app.py`, `requirements.txt`, `requirements-ai.txt`, `.env.example`, `.dockerignore`, `Dockerfile`, and `frontend/Dockerfile`.
- Updated segment-save validation/caption regeneration and made job-detail access require a user cookie; internal workers use `get_job(..., internal=True)`.

### Active
- Replace the generic starter `README.md` with accurate setup, usage, deployment, and limitation documentation.
- Run Python syntax/import checks and frontend install/build; fix any issues.
- Review integration and deployment behavior, including the Docker setup and Gradio MVP.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Write the project README with local setup, AI model/runtime requirements, Docker instructions, and known limitations.
2. Run Python checks and frontend dependency install/build; resolve any errors.
3. Review the final API/UI workflow and accurately report remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `backend/pipeline.py`: FFmpeg and AI dubbing pipeline.
- `backend/main.py`: FastAPI endpoints, SQLite jobs/quota, threaded worker, and segment saving.
- `gradio_app.py`: Single-file Gradio MVP.
- `frontend/app/page.tsx`: Dashboard, progress, results, and transcript editing UI.
- `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`: Upload and dubbing configuration form.
- `frontend/lib/api.ts`: Frontend API types and helpers.
- `requirements.txt`: Lightweight backend and Gradio dependencies.
- `requirements-ai.txt`: Optional AI/media dependencies.
- `Dockerfile`: API container.
- `frontend/Dockerfile`: Next.js container.
- `.env.example`: Backend and frontend environment variable examples.
- `README.md`: Still contains generic starter content; needs replacement.

## Important Context
- Backend defaults to port `8000`; frontend runs on port `3000` and defaults to `http://localhost:8000`.
- FFmpeg/ffprobe are required; AI model packages load at runtime, and edge-tts requires internet access. Music preservation requires Demucs.
- Voice cloning is not implemented. Transcript edits update downloadable captions but not audio or burned-in subtitles.
- Changes are uncommitted; Python checks and frontend build have not yet been run.

60: def segments_from_words(words: list[Any], transcript: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
61:     segments: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
62:     chunk: list[Any] = []
63:     for word in words:
64:         chunk.append(word)
65:         text = str(getattr(word, "word", "")).strip()
66:         gap = getattr(word, "start", 0) - getattr(chunk[-2], "end", 0) if len(chunk) > 1 else 0
67:         if (re.search(r"[.!?。؟।]$", text) and len(chunk) >= 3) or gap > 0.9 or len(chunk) >= 22:
68:             segments.append(_word_segment(chunk))
69:             chunk = []
70:     if chunk:

73:         segments = [{"start": 0.0, "end": 0.0, "text": transcript.strip()}]

input.content:
# Voxora Dubbing Studio

A free, open-source MVP for dubbing short audio and video clips. It combines a FastAPI/SQLite job API, a responsive Next.js dashboard, and a single-file Gradio interface. The processing pipeline uses FFmpeg, Faster-Whisper for transcription, NLLB for translation, and generated text-to-speech voices.

> **Important:** This is an experimental, single-user/local-first MVP—not a hardened public service. The dashboard's “Text to Speech”, “Speech to Text”, “Voice Library”, and “Voice Cloning” pages are placeholders; the supported workflow is audio/video dubbing. Voice cloning is not implemented. Generated speech uses Microsoft Edge TTS voices through the `edge-tts` package, so synthesis requires an internet connection and sends translated text to that service. Review the applicable service terms and privacy requirements before use.

## Features

- Upload audio or video, or record audio in a supported browser.
- Transcribe with word-level timing, translate to one or more target languages, and generate timed speech.
- Choose generated voice gender and speech speed; optionally provide a comma-separated glossary.
- Optionally preserve background music using Demucs or burn subtitles into the output video.
- Download MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT outputs; edit the transcript/translation and regenerate downloadable captions.
- Track anonymous per-browser daily usage (30 minutes by default), view job progress, and delete completed/failed jobs.
- Responsive dashboard with light and dark themes, plus a simpler Gradio MVP.

Supported languages: Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Urdu, and English. Source language can also be auto-detected.

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+ (Python 3.11 is used in the Docker image).
- Node.js 20+ and npm for the dashboard.
- FFmpeg **and** FFprobe available on `PATH`.
- For AI processing, install `requirements-ai.txt`. PyTorch and model downloads can require substantial disk space and memory; CPU processing is supported but can be slow. The first run downloads the Whisper and NLLB models.
- Internet access is needed for initial model downloads and Edge TTS speech synthesis. Demucs is needed to preserve background music.

## Local setup

Run commands from the repository root. In one terminal, set up and run the API:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
# Linux/macOS
source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements-ai.txt
cp .env.example .env  # optional; defaults also work
uvicorn backend.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

On Windows, copy `.env.example` to `.env` manually if needed. Install FFmpeg separately and ensure `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`.

In another terminal, run the web app:

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
# Optional: set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL in frontend/.env.local for a non-default API URL.
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:3000>. The API health check is at <http://localhost:8000/api/health> and the interactive API docs are at <http://localhost:8000/docs>.

The lightweight API/Gradio dependencies can instead be installed with `pip install -r requirements.txt`. To run the single-file Gradio MVP, from the repository root:

```bash
python gradio_app.py
```

Then open <http://localhost:7860>. It uses the same AI pipeline and therefore still needs the AI dependencies, FFmpeg, model downloads, and internet for speech synthesis.

## Docker

The backend image installs FFmpeg and the optional AI stack. Persist its `/data` volume so uploaded files, generated outputs, and the SQLite database survive container replacement:

```bash
docker build -t voxora-api .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
  -e DUB_STORAGE=/data \
  -e DUB_DB=/data/dubbing.sqlite3 \
  -v voxora-data:/data \
  voxora-api
```

Build and run the frontend in a second terminal. The API URL is embedded at **build time** by Next.js; use an address reachable from the user's browser (not the Docker-internal service name):

```bash
docker build --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 \
  -t voxora-web ./frontend
docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 voxora-web
```

Open <http://localhost:3000>. If the browser-facing API origin differs from `http://localhost:8000`, set `CORS_ORIGINS` on the API container to a comma-separated list containing the frontend origin, and rebuild the frontend with the correct `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. For example, on a LAN use the machine's reachable hostname/IP in both settings. Terminate TLS with a trusted reverse proxy before remote use; cookies are currently configured for local HTTP (`SameSite=Lax`, not `Secure`).

The frontend Dockerfile currently uses `npm install`; there is no checked-in npm lockfile. For reproducible deployments, generate and commit `frontend/package-lock.json`, then use `npm ci` in the image build.

## Configuration

Copy `.env.example` and adjust values for your setup:

| Variable | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DUB_STORAGE` | `backend/storage` when run from the repo root | Directory for uploads, outputs, and temporary job data. |
| `DUB_DB` | `<DUB_STORAGE>/dubbing.sqlite3` | SQLite database path. |
| `DAILY_MINUTES` | `30` | Anonymous user's daily upload quota in minutes. |
| `DUB_WORKERS` | `1` | Background job worker count; larger values use more CPU/RAM. |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000` | Comma-separated allowed browser origins. |
| `WHISPER_MODEL` | `small` | Faster-Whisper model name. Larger models need more memory and run slower. |
| `WHISPER_DEVICE` | `cpu` | Whisper device, e.g. `cpu` or a configured GPU device. |
| `WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE` | `int8` on CPU | Faster-Whisper compute type; choose a compatible value for the device. |
| `NLLB_MODEL` | `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M` | Hugging Face translation model identifier/path. |
| `DEMUCS_MODEL` | `htdemucs` | Demucs model used for vocal/background separation. |

AI model weights are downloaded/cached by their libraries; make sure the runtime user can write to the relevant model cache. Container storage `/data` is separate from those caches unless configured otherwise.

## Limits and behavior

- Upload limit: 2 GB. Media duration limit: 60 minutes. The default daily quota is 30 minutes per anonymous browser identity and resets at local midnight.
- Job identity is an anonymous cookie, **not an account or authentication system**. Clearing/changing the cookie loses access to that browser's job history; this must not be treated as secure access control for a multi-user/public deployment.
- Jobs run in a thread pool in the API process. They are not distributed or persisted as a durable queue; restarting the process interrupts active work. Use one API process with SQLite for this MVP.
- Enabling music preservation requires Demucs; the backend fails the job with an installation hint if unavailable.
- Audio and video output is produced for each target language. Music is preserved only when requested. Burning subtitles applies to video output.
- Editing transcript text updates the stored transcript and downloadable SRT/VTT files. It does **not** regenerate dubbed audio or subtitles already burned into a video.
- Voice-cloning controls only collect a consent acknowledgement for the UI/API; cloning is not implemented and no cloned voice is generated.
- Translation and voice synthesis quality/timing can vary. Review outputs before publishing; do not assume generated content is a faithful or legally cleared translation.

## Privacy and rights

Uploads and results are stored on the configured backend storage and remain until the job is deleted or the storage is removed. The app does not currently have automated retention cleanup, user accounts, encryption-at-rest management, or production-grade authentication. Use only media and voices you have rights to use. Avoid uploading sensitive content to a deployment you do not control, and review the policies of all model and speech services used.

## License

No project license file is included yet. Add a license before redistributing this repository or presenting the project as licensed open source. Each model, dependency, voice, and external speech service may have separate terms; verify them independently.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the free, open-source AI audio/video dubbing app, including its Gradio MVP, FastAPI backend, and Next.js UI; document setup and deployment and verify the build.

## Requirements
- Avoid paid APIs, API keys, and credit cards; make no clarification requests.
- Support media upload, multiple target languages, music preservation, timed dubbing, MP4/MP3 and SRT/VTT downloads, transcript editing, quota tracking, responsive UI, themes, and voice-rights consent.
- Include dependency manifests, Docker setup, `.env.example`, and local/free deployment instructions.

## Decisions
- Prioritize the dubbing app over the conflicting game request.
- Use FastAPI, SQLite, threaded jobs, and Next.js; keep AI dependencies separate from lightweight requirements.
- Voice cloning is not implemented; the UI discloses standard voices are used.
- Transcript edits regenerate downloadable SRT/VTT captions, but do not change audio or subtitles already burned into video.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the dubbing pipeline, API, Gradio MVP, and Next.js dashboard, including job management, downloads, quotas, transcript edits, and responsive/theme UI.
- Added Dockerfiles, `.env.example`, dependency manifests, and replaced generic starter README content with setup, Docker, limitations, and privacy documentation.
- `python -m py_compile backend/main.py backend/pipeline.py gradio_app.py` passed.
- `npm install` completed and created `frontend/package-lock.json`.

### Active
- Fix the frontend production build type error in `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`.
- Resolve or assess frontend dependency audit findings before deployment.
- Complete runtime/integration checks after installing backend dependencies.

### Blocked
- Backend import/runtime check could not run because `fastapi` is not installed (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi'`).
- `npm run build` fails during type checking: `CreateDub.tsx:13` passes a `string[]` as the second argument to `new File(...)`.
- `npm audit --omit=dev` reports one critical Next.js vulnerability and one high PostCSS vulnerability; suggested `npm audit fix --force` requires a breaking Next.js upgrade.

## Next Move
1. Fix the `new File(...)` arguments in `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`, then rerun `npm run build`.
2. Review compatible dependency upgrades and regenerate the lockfile; rerun npm audit.
3. Install `requirements-ai.txt` or at least `requirements.txt`, then check backend imports and exercise the local workflow.
4. Review README commands and Docker behavior against the verified setup.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: Setup, Docker deployment, limitations, and privacy documentation.
- `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`: Current TypeScript build failure.
- `frontend/package.json`: Frontend dependency versions and scripts.
- `frontend/package-lock.json`: Generated dependency lockfile.
- `backend/main.py`: API, quota, jobs, and downloads.
- `backend/pipeline.py`: Transcription, translation, synthesis, and media processing.
- `gradio_app.py`: Single-file Gradio MVP.
- `requirements.txt`: Lightweight backend/Gradio dependencies.
- `requirements-ai.txt`: Optional AI/media dependencies.
- `Dockerfile`: Backend container.
- `frontend/Dockerfile`: Frontend container.
- `.env.example`: Runtime configuration examples.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status` also showed untracked `__pycache__/`.
- Backend defaults to port `8000`; frontend runs on port `3000`; Gradio runs on port `7860`.
- FFmpeg/FFprobe are required. AI models download on first use; Edge TTS requires internet, and Demucs is required for music preservation.
- Anonymous cookie identity is not authentication; do not expose this MVP publicly without additional security measures.
- README local API command is `cd backend` then `uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`.

1: # Voxora Dubbing Studio
2: 
3: A free, open-source MVP for dubbing short audio and video clips. It combines a FastAPI/SQLite job API, a responsive Next.js dashboard, and a single-file Gradio interface. The processing pipeline uses FFmpeg, Faster-Whisper for transcription, NLLB for translation, and generated text-to-speech voices.
4: 
5: > **Important:** This is an experimental, single-user/local-first MVP—not a hardened public service. The dashboard's “Text to Speech”, “Speech to Text”, “Voice Library”, and “Voice Cloning” pages are placeholders; the supported workflow is audio/video dubbing. Voice cloning is not implemented. Generated speech uses Microsoft Edge TTS voices through the `edge-tts` package, so synthesis requires an internet connection and sends translated text to that service. Review the applicable service terms and privacy requirements before use.
6: 
7: ## Features
8: 
9: - Upload audio or video, or record audio in a supported browser.
10: - Transcribe with word-level timing, translate to one or more target languages, and generate timed speech.
11: - Choose generated voice gender and speech speed; optionally provide a comma-separated glossary.
12: - Optionally preserve background music using Demucs or burn subtitles into the output video.
13: - Download MP4, MP3, SRT, and VTT outputs; edit the transcript/translation and regenerate downloadable captions.
14: - Track anonymous per-browser daily usage (30 minutes by default), view job progress, and delete completed/failed jobs.
15: - Responsive dashboard with light and dark themes, plus a simpler Gradio MVP.
16: 
17: Supported languages: Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Urdu, and English. Source language can also be auto-detected.
18: 
19: ## Requirements
20: 
21: - Python 3.10+ (Python 3.11 is used in the Docker image).
22: - Node.js 20+ and npm for the dashboard.
23: - FFmpeg **and** FFprobe available on `PATH`.
24: - For AI processing, install `requirements-ai.txt`. PyTorch and model downloads can require substantial disk space and memory; CPU processing is supported but can be slow. The first run downloads the Whisper and NLLB models.
25: - Internet access is needed for initial model downloads and Edge TTS speech synthesis. Demucs is needed to preserve background music.
26: 
27: ## Local setup
28: 
29: Run commands from the repository root. In one terminal, set up and run the API:
30: 
31: ```bash
32: python -m venv .venv
33: # Linux/macOS
34: source .venv/bin/activate
35: # Windows PowerShell: .venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1
36: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
37: pip install -r requirements-ai.txt
38: cp .env.example .env  # optional; defaults also work
39: cd backend
40: uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
41: ```
42: 
43: On Windows, copy `.env.example` to `.env` manually if needed. Install FFmpeg separately and ensure `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are on `PATH`.
44: 
45: In another terminal, run the web app:
46: 
47: ```bash
48: cd frontend
49: npm install
50: # Optional: set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL in frontend/.env.local for a non-default API URL.
51: npm run dev
52: ```
53: 
54: Open <http://localhost:3000>. The API health check is at <http://localhost:8000/api/health> and the interactive API docs are at <http://localhost:8000/docs>.
55: 
56: The lightweight API/Gradio dependencies can instead be installed with `pip install -r requirements.txt`. To run the single-file Gradio MVP, from the repository root:
57: 
58: ```bash
59: python gradio_app.py
60: ```
61: 
62: Then open <http://localhost:7860>. It uses the same AI pipeline and therefore still needs the AI dependencies, FFmpeg, model downloads, and internet for speech synthesis.
63: 
64: ## Docker
65: 
66: The backend image installs FFmpeg and the optional AI stack. Persist its `/data` volume so uploaded files, generated outputs, and the SQLite database survive container replacement:
67: 
68: ```bash
69: docker build -t voxora-api .
70: docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
71:   -e DUB_STORAGE=/data \
72:   -e DUB_DB=/data/dubbing.sqlite3 \
73:   -v voxora-data:/data \
74:   voxora-api
75: ```
76: 
77: Build and run the frontend in a second terminal. The API URL is embedded at **build time** by Next.js; use an address reachable from the user's browser (not the Docker-internal service name):
78: 
79: ```bash
80: docker build --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 \
81:   -t voxora-web ./frontend
82: docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 voxora-web
83: ```
84: 
85: Open <http://localhost:3000>. If the browser-facing API origin differs from `http://localhost:8000`, set `CORS_ORIGINS` on the API container to a comma-separated list containing the frontend origin, and rebuild the frontend with the correct `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. For example, on a LAN use the machine's reachable hostname/IP in both settings. Terminate TLS with a trusted reverse proxy before remote use; cookies are currently configured for local HTTP (`SameSite=Lax`, not `Secure`).
86: 
87: The frontend Dockerfile currently uses `npm install`; there is no checked-in npm lockfile. For reproducible deployments, generate and commit `frontend/package-lock.json`, then use `npm ci` in the image build.
88: 
89: ## Configuration
90: 
91: Copy `.env.example` and adjust values for your setup:
92: 
93: | Variable | Default | Description |
94: | --- | --- | --- |
95: | `DUB_STORAGE` | `backend/storage` when run from the repo root | Directory for uploads, outputs, and temporary job data. |
96: | `DUB_DB` | `<DUB_STORAGE>/dubbing.sqlite3` | SQLite database path. |
97: | `DAILY_MINUTES` | `30` | Anonymous user's daily upload quota in minutes. |
98: | `DUB_WORKERS` | `1` | Background job worker count; larger values use more CPU/RAM. |
99: | `CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000` | Comma-separated allowed browser origins. |
100: | `WHISPER_MODEL` | `small` | Faster-Whisper model name. Larger models need more memory and run slower. |
101: | `WHISPER_DEVICE` | `cpu` | Whisper device, e.g. `cpu` or a configured GPU device. |
102: | `WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE` | `int8` on CPU | Faster-Whisper compute type; choose a compatible value for the device. |
103: | `NLLB_MODEL` | `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M` | Hugging Face translation model identifier/path. |
104: | `DEMUCS_MODEL` | `htdemucs` | Demucs model used for vocal/background separation. |
105: 
106: AI model weights are downloaded/cached by their libraries; make sure the runtime user can write to the relevant model cache. Container storage `/data` is separate from those caches unless configured otherwise.
107: 
108: ## Limits and behavior
109: 
110: - Upload limit: 2 GB. Media duration limit: 60 minutes. The default daily quota is 30 minutes per anonymous browser identity and resets at local midnight.
111: - Job identity is an anonymous cookie, **not an account or authentication system**. Clearing/changing the cookie loses access to that browser's job history; this must not be treated as secure access control for a multi-user/public deployment.
112: - Jobs run in a thread pool in the API process. They are not distributed or persisted as a durable queue; restarting the process interrupts active work. Use one API process with SQLite for this MVP.
113: - Enabling music preservation requires Demucs; the backend fails the job with an installation hint if unavailable.
114: - Audio and video output is produced for each target language. Music is preserved only when requested. Burning subtitles applies to video output.
115: - Editing transcript text updates the stored transcript and downloadable SRT/VTT files. It does **not** regenerate dubbed audio or subtitles already burned into a video.
116: - Voice-cloning controls only collect a consent acknowledgement for the UI/API; cloning is not implemented and no cloned voice is generated.
117: - Translation and voice synthesis quality/timing can vary. Review outputs before publishing; do not assume generated content is a faithful or legally cleared translation.
118: 
119: ## Privacy and rights
120: 
121: Uploads and results are stored on the configured backend storage and remain until the job is deleted or the storage is removed. The app does not currently have automated retention cleanup, user accounts, encryption-at-rest management, or production-grade authentication. Use only media and voices you have rights to use. Avoid uploading sensitive content to a deployment you do not control, and review the policies of all model and speech services used.

## Objective
- Complete the free, open-source AI audio/video dubbing app across its Gradio MVP, FastAPI backend, and Next.js UI; document setup and deployment and verify the build.

## Requirements
- Avoid paid APIs, API keys, and credit cards; do not ask for clarification.
- Support media upload, multiple target languages, music preservation, timed dubbing, MP4/MP3 and SRT/VTT downloads, transcript editing, quota tracking, responsive UI, themes, and voice-rights consent.
- Include dependency manifests, Docker setup, `.env.example`, and local/free deployment instructions.

## Decisions
- Prioritize the dubbing app over the conflicting game request.
- Use FastAPI, SQLite, threaded jobs, and Next.js; keep AI dependencies separate from lightweight requirements.
- Voice cloning is not implemented; the UI discloses standard voices are used.
- Transcript edits regenerate downloadable SRT/VTT captions, but do not change audio or subtitles already burned into video.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the dubbing pipeline, API, Gradio MVP, and Next.js dashboard, including job management, downloads, quotas, transcript edits, and responsive/theme UI.
- Added Dockerfiles, `.env.example`, dependency manifests, and setup, Docker, limitations, and privacy documentation.
- Fixed the `new File(...)` TypeScript argument error in `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`; `npm run build` passed before the latest dependency upgrade.
- Installed lightweight backend dependencies into `/tmp/opencode/dubbing-venv`; importing `backend/main.py` succeeded and returned a healthy service with 14 routes.
- Python compilation passed previously for `backend/main.py`, `backend/pipeline.py`, and `gradio_app.py`.

### Active
- Validate the latest frontend dependency upgrade (`next@^15.5.29`, `postcss@^8.5.23`): rerun the production build and inspect the audit findings.
- Update the stale README and frontend Dockerfile to use the generated lockfile (`npm ci`).
- Exercise backend and Gradio runtime flows; AI media processing remains untested.

### Blocked
- `npm install next@^15.5.29 postcss@^8.5.23` reported two vulnerabilities (one moderate, one high); details and fixes are not yet assessed.
- Full AI pipeline verification needs optional AI dependencies, model downloads, FFmpeg/FFprobe, and Edge TTS connectivity.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and inspect `npm audit` after the Next.js/PostCSS upgrade.
2. Update `frontend/Dockerfile` to use `npm ci` and correct the README statement that no lockfile exists.
3. Run backend/Gradio checks and, if feasible, test an end-to-end media workflow.
4. Review the final README commands and Docker behavior against the verified setup.

## Relevant Files
- `frontend/components/CreateDub.tsx`: Fixed `File` construction for microphone recordings.
- `frontend/package.json`: Updated Next.js and PostCSS dependency ranges.
- `frontend/package-lock.json`: Generated lockfile; dependency audit remains pending.
- `frontend/Dockerfile`: Still uses `npm install`.
- `README.md`: Setup/deployment documentation; contains stale lockfile guidance.
- `backend/main.py`: FastAPI API, job handling, quotas, and downloads.
- `backend/pipeline.py`: Transcription, translation, synthesis, and media processing.
- `gradio_app.py`: Gradio MVP.
- `requirements.txt`: Lightweight backend dependencies.
- `requirements-ai.txt`: Optional AI/media dependencies.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status` showed modified `README.md` and multiple untracked app/config files, including `frontend/` and `__pycache__/`.
- Backend defaults to port `8000`; frontend runs on port `3000`; Gradio runs on port `7860`.
- FFmpeg/FFprobe are required. AI models download on first use; Edge TTS requires internet, and Demucs is required for music preservation.
- Anonymous cookie identity is not authentication; do not expose this MVP publicly without additional security measures.
